lines: We went there, then we came back here. I liked the back here part best.
Home again, whole enough to thank you properly. That matters.
We came back with the village still ahead of us. I'll count that as good work.
I followed you out and you brought me back. Nice and complete.
The road was long, but none of my parts fell off.
I worried about getting home until our roofs came over the hill.
You kept the dangerous things on the outside of our little group.
I did not know where we were half the time. You did, which worked out well.
My feet are tired and the rest of me is pleased.
I saw a great many places. This one still has my bed, so it wins.
Thank you for waiting whenever I stopped to tie the same boot again.
I brought every worry home unopened.
You said we would make it back. I saved believing you for the difficult parts.
I only got lost while looking directly at you once.
That journey was almost sensible from beginning to end.
I am glad I trusted you with the road.
We returned before anyone gave my sunny corner away.
I learned that staying close is easier when the guide remembers to look behind.
Next time I will pack less nonsense and more bread.
Home feels extra home-shaped after following you that far.
I got bonked on the trip. Home is better when fewer things bonk me.
I made it home, but the road took more from me than it should have.
Next time, let us return with fewer marks and better choices.
This bruise has started telling the story before I do.
I followed you home on one good leg and a very determined other leg.
You got me back, but I would like an explanation for the arrow-shaped part.
The healer says I will mend. The healer also made a face I did not enjoy.
I trusted you to keep me safe. Mostly safe is doing too much work in that sentence.
My ribs hurt when I laugh, so please be less funny for a while.
I am home, alive, and shaped almost the same as before.
The road left a mark. Several marks, if we are counting carefully.
You helped me walk the last stretch. I remember that more kindly than the fall.
Next time danger appears, I would like us to notice it before it notices me.
I need rest, soup, and a journey that already ended.
We made it back. My shoulder is still arriving.
I am grateful you did not leave me there, even if I wish we had never reached there.
These bandages make me look experienced. I would rather be inexperienced.
I thought the worst part was getting hurt. Walking home corrected me.
Please say the next trip involves fewer weapons and more sitting.
I will forgive the road after it stops aching in my knees.
I thought following meant you were on my side. That was the important bit.
Following you was trust. What happened after was something else.
A guide who strikes from close by leaves the longest mark.
You asked me to come, then made me fear the person I followed.
I watched the road for monsters. I should have watched you.
Do not call it a mistake. Mistakes do not keep swinging.
I was far from home because I believed you.
You knew I would stay close. You used that against me.
I can be foolish without deserving what you did.
The wound will close before the trust does.
I followed your back because I thought it was safe to do so.
You brought me away from every familiar door and then turned on me.
I remember exactly when the journey stopped being ours.
You do not get to smile this into a smaller thing.
I made it home despite you, not because of you.
Next time you ask me to follow, the answer already knows it is no.
I trusted your directions. I will not trust your reasons again.
The road was dangerous, but you were the danger standing nearest.
I may forgive slowly. I will not forget quickly.
Leave me alone. You have guided me far enough.
The boat moved and I did not have to. I liked that part.
The boat did its part. I am still deciding whether the rest of the plan did.
Water carried us home, which is more than I expected from that journey.
I stepped onto land and immediately forgave the ground for everything.
You steered us back without arguing with the river. Good choice.
The boat wobbled, I wobbled, and somehow we canceled each other out.
I kept looking for the road until I remembered it was underneath the water.
We reached the village with the boat still below us. Excellent boating.
My legs still think the floor is moving. Please tell the floor to stop.
I liked seeing our roofs from the water. They looked less likely to tip.
Thank you for rowing when my arms became decorative.
Every fish we passed knew more about the trip than I did.
I held the side so firmly that the side may miss me.
The river took the long way home, but at least it knew one.
I worried about sinking until we were close enough to worry about docking.
You found the landing. I was prepared to live in the boat by then.
Next time I am bringing a cushion and fewer thoughts about deep water.
Getting out was my finest step of the whole journey.
I did not fall overboard once. I would like that written down.
The boat is empty, we are home, and the water may continue without us.
